    31  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    32      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (maxNatSize : Nat) (ds : Array Declaration)
    33      (accepted : (checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds).isOk) :
    34      ∃ model, IsModel V model (· ∈ constantsOf ds.toList) := by
    35    cases h : checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds with
    36    | error e => rw [h] at accepted; cases accepted

    38      obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) h
    39      exact ⟨_, isModel_of_envModelM m (Cached.checkDecls_recordsStored h)⟩

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/name.rs#L641-L653
   641  pub fn render(n: &Name) -> Vec<u32> {
   642      match &n.0.kind {
   643          NameKind::Anonymous => {
   644              const A: [u32; 11] = [91, 97, 110, 111, 110, 121, 109, 111, 117, 115, 93];
   645              crate::kernel::core_types::code_points(&A)
   646          }
   647          _ => {
   648              let cs = component_list(n, Vec::new());
   649              let k = cs.len();
   650              display_acc_finish(render_from(&cs, k, display_acc_empty()))
   651          }
   652      }
   653  }

== proof/ConRon/MainTheorem.lean#L10-L100
    10  /-!
    11  # `ConRon.MainTheorem` — the main theorems about the binary (task #171, DESIGN.md §3.9)
    12  
    13  The twin of `ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean`: the same theorem names, in the same order, with the
    14  same statements word for word, but con-leche's run premise `ModelIO.CanGive (Driver.runArgs
    15  args) fs 0` is con-ron's `ConRon.CanGive args fs 0` (`MainTheorem/Model.lean`): the extracted
    16  driver `driver::cli::run_args` exits 0 on the argument list `args` at the MODEL instance of the
    17  trait `CheckerIo`, `Model.snapshotIo fs`, from some oracle.  The model is con-ron's `ModelIO`:
    18  its file operations answer from the snapshot `fs` (a failure where `fs` has no answer, and at a
    19  path that is not a well-formed string); every escape that answers a value (the help's and the
    20  scheduler's exit codes, the hardware thread count, the copies' error) takes its answer from the
    21  oracle, so any value of its type is possible; the worker map folds each job over the claims the
    22  oracle picks; the code map runs every job; the notifications do nothing.  That the model
    23  answers as `fs` and keeps the two maps' contracts are theorems about it
    24  (`Model.snapshotIo_answersAs`, `snapshotIo_poolSound`, `snapshotIo_codesSound`), which the walks
    25  use through the instance-generic `CanGiveConforming` (`CanGive.conforming`).
    26  
    27  **What is proved, and what is trusted** (con-leche's `ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean`, its
    28  module doc, says the same of its binary; OVERVIEW §3.1 is this paragraph's table).  The
    29  theorems say: every run of the model that exits 0 implies the statement.  The binary's `main`
    30  (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is the argument list's code points (an argument that is
    31  not UTF-8 is exit 3), the checking thread, the same generic `run_args` at the binary's instance
    32  `StdIo` (`crates/con-ron/src/std_io.rs`), the flush and the exit with the code `run_args`
    33  returned; those lines are read, not proved.  The code is computed by the extracted driver and
    34  returned outside every escape.  A run of the binary that exits 0 is one of the model's runs,
    35  with that code, if
    36  
    37  1. every file operation the run PERFORMS answered as one snapshot `fs` of the files: the same
    38     value where the model has one, and a failure where the model fails (`StdIo` fails at a path
    39     with a code point that is not a character, at a real path that is not valid UTF-8, at a size
    40     its file's contents do not end at, and at a path whose file was replaced between two
    41     openings of it; it reads every byte range through the run's one handle of the file, up to
    42     where a read finds the end).  Those checks catch a path replaced by another file, not a file
    43     rewritten in place: that the files do not change during the run is assumed, as con-leche
    44     assumes it, not enforced;
    45     and on the binary's platform the Rust's spelling of a module's file (`files::mod_file_of`) is
    46     upstream's (`modFile`), which the logic cannot decide (`System.FilePath`'s `/` reads the
    47     opaque `System.Platform.isWindows`), so the model also fails where they would differ;
    48  2. the escapes and notifications do not change what the file operations see (none writes a file
    49     a check reads: they print, read the clock, count threads, keep what the run built, and start
    50     the scheduler, whose workers only read) and do not end the process with exit code 0;
    51  3. the two maps' actual runs are some oracle's: the worker map (`pool::parallel_all`) runs each
    52     worker from the job's first state over the positions it claims, in increasing order, every
    53     position claimed, and answers `Ok` only when every step did, which is an argument about its
    54     control flow; the code map runs every module's step and answers their codes in order; and
    55  4. Rust, its standard library and Aeneas run and model the code as written.
    56  
    57  The argument is then con-leche's: the extracted code is the same at both instances; at every file
    58  operation the run performs, the binary's answer is, by (1) and (2), the model's; at every escape
    59  the binary's answer is SOME value of its type, and the model has an oracle that gives it (the
    60  oracle is chosen after the run, answer by answer); at each map, by (3), an oracle's claims give
    61  the binary's answer.  So, by induction along the run, a run of the binary that reaches the exit
    62  with 0 is one of the model's runs, and what is proved of all of those holds of it.  Calls the run
    63  does not perform constrain nothing.
    64  
    65  What differs from con-leche: an ORACLE in the instance's state where con-leche has a
    66  non-determinism monad (Aeneas models a trait method as a function, so "any outcome" is "the
    67  oracle's", the oracle existentially chosen); and POSITIONAL reads (`read_range`) where con-leche
    68  opens a handle and reads it forward (the model's `ModelIO.read` slices the file from the
    69  handle's position; con-ron's slice is at the offset the reader passes, the reader's own
    70  position).  One `&self` escape answers a value, `worker_copies`, inside the code map where the
    71  instance is shared: in the model its answer is the oracle's function of its arguments, so it
    72  claims that two calls with the same arguments at one state agree, which the binary's
    73  (deterministic in its arguments) does; and it can only turn an accept into a failure.
    74  
    75  **Several processes.**  `main_modular`, `main_modular_compare` and
    76  `main_modular_compare_no_False` are about several runs of the binary: they assume (1) to (4) of
    77  every run, with one snapshot for all of them, as con-leche's do.
    78  
    79  **The proofs.**  Each theorem is a walk of the extracted driver and a conclusion.  The walk
    80  (`MainTheorem/Driver.lean`, `CompareJson.lean`, `Oleans.lean`, `Modular.lean`,
    81  `CompareOleans.lean`, `CompareModular.lean`, over the argument parses of `Args.lean`,
    82  `ModArgs.lean` and `CmpArgs.lean`) inverts `run_args` at the theorem's argument list, one
    83  lemma per driver function, down to the calls of the verified stages, and hands them to the
    84  staged lemmas of `MainTheorem/Stages.lean`: one premise per call, Theorem 2 (the Rust refines the
    85  twin), then Theorem 1 (the twin refines con-leche's pure checker).  `MainTheorem/Conclusions.lean`
    86  turns the staged conclusions into con-leche's words with con-leche's own soundness theorems:
    87  
    88  | theorem | the walk | the conclusion |
    89  |---|---|---|
    90  | `main_json_model`, `main_no_False` | `json_stages_of_canGive` | `json_model_of_stages`, `json_no_False_of_stages` |
    91  | `main_compare_json_model` | `compare_json_stages_of_canGive` | `compare_json_model_of_stages` |
    92  | `main_oleans` | `oleans_of_canGive` | `oleans_model_of_stages_dec` |
    93  | `main_compare_model` | `compare_of_canGive` | `compare_model_of_stages_dec` |
    94  | `main_modular`, `main_modular_one` | `modular_of_canGive`, `modular_one_of_canGive` | `Stages.model_modular_of` |
    95  | `main_modular_compare`, `main_modular_compare_one`, `main_modular_compare_no_False` | `modular_cmp_facts_of_canGive`, `modular_cmp_one_of_canGive` | `cmp_family`, `cmp_no_False` |
    96  
    97  The proofs use the axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` and
    98  `PINS_TEXT._native.decide.ax_1`, the one Aeneas spends on the embedded pin text's definition,
    99  and no other (the census at the end of this file).
   100  -/

   169  open ConLeche ConLeche.Frontend in
   170  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean:109-122 main_modular —
   171  **An accepted modular check has a family of models**: on a snapshot where `--check-graph
   172  --search-path=<dirs> -- <root>` exits 0 and every module of the headers' closure of `root` has
   173  an exit 0 of `--olean --module`, every module of the closure has a model of its constants, and
   174  the models agree on what the modules see of each other. -/
   175  theorem main_modular (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] {dirs root : String} {r : Name} {fs : FS}
   176      (hr : Olean.parseModName root = some r)
   177      (h : ConRon.CanGive ["--check-graph", "--search-path=" ++ dirs, "--", root] fs 0)
   178      (hwork : ∀ m', Olean.HdrClosure (Driver.searchPathOf dirs) fs [r] m' → ∃ root',
   179        Olean.parseModName root' = some m' ∧
   180          ConRon.CanGive ["--olean", "--module", "--search-path=" ++ dirs, "--", root'] fs 0) :
   181      ∃ model : Name → (Name → List Nat → V),
   182        (∀ m, Olean.InClosure (Driver.searchPathOf dirs) fs #[r] m →
   183          IsModel V (model m) (Olean.moduleConstants (Driver.searchPathOf dirs) fs m)) ∧
   184        (∀ m n m', Olean.InClosure (Driver.searchPathOf dirs) fs #[r] m →
   185          Olean.Sees (Driver.searchPathOf dirs) fs m n m' → model m n = model m' n) :=
   186    modular_of_canGive V hr h.conforming
   187      fun m hm => (hwork m hm).imp fun _ h => ⟨h.1, h.2.conforming⟩

   210  theorem main_modular_compare (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] {T D c s : String} {C S : Name}
   211      {fs : FS} (hc : Olean.parseModName c = some C) (hs : Olean.parseModName s = some S)
   212      (hgraph : ConRon.CanGive ["--check-graph", "--compare",
   213        "--trusted-search-path=" ++ T, "--search-path=" ++ D, "--", c, s] fs 0)
   214      (hwork : ∀ m, Olean.HdrClosure
   215          (⟨C, S, Driver.searchPathOf T, Driver.searchPathOf D, none⟩ : Driver.CmpReq).solRoots fs

== proof/ConRon/MainTheorem/Stages.lean#L25-L95
    25  /-!
    26  # `ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages` — the staged lemmas: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    27  
    28  The main theorems (`ConRon/MainTheorem.lean`) are proved from these lemmas.  Each states, for
    29  one mode of the binary, what follows from the verified calls the driver makes in that mode:
    30  one premise per call, in the driver's order, each starting from the state the previous one
    31  left and the first from the binary's own start values.  The driver walks of
    32  `MainTheorem/*.lean` take an exit 0 of the extracted driver `run_args` to exactly these
    33  premises, and `MainTheorem/Conclusions.lean` turns the conclusions here into con-leche's words.
    34  This is the one module that imports both `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and
    35  `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2, (C) ⇒ (B)):
    36  
    37  * `model_exists` / `no_False_declaration` — a lean4export file (`driver::check_main`);
    38  * `no_False_oleans` / `model_exists_oleans` — the same on `--olean` (`check_main::check_oleans`);
    39  * `model_exists_compare` / `no_False_compare` and `model_exists_oleans_compare` /
    40    `no_False_oleans_compare` — a challenge checked with its axioms justified by a solution
    41    (`driver::compare_json`, `driver::compare`; §4b and §4c), about the challenge alone;
    42  * `model_modular` and its compared forms — the graph check and a module's worker
    43    (`driver::graph`, `driver::worker`, `driver::modular`, `driver::compare_module`).
    44  
    45  The calls are marked `// ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: <premise>` in the driver's Rust.
    46  
    47  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    48  
    49  On a lean4export file the driver (`crates/con-ron-core/src/driver/check_main.rs`) calls, in
    50  this order, on one `AState` made from `AState::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    51  
    52      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source (FileChunks)
    53        → prepare_d → decode_embedded → intern_all_pins → (the check phase)
    54  
    55  **The check phase** (`check_main::check_phase`) builds the stream's index from the records
    56  (`stream_index::build_index`), freezes the tier with the index in it (`checker::freeze_tier`),
    57  runs every record's job on the instance's worker map, and thaws the tier.  The lemmas take one
    58  premise per step (`h6` the index, `h7` the freeze, `h8` the map), which `poolAccepts_intro`
    59  assembles into `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  `h8` is the worker map's
    60  contract (`PoolSound`) at the driver's step (`ParallelAll` at `jobStep`): index lists, one per
    61  worker, covering every job, each in increasing order, and for each a fold of `run_job` over its
    62  indices from `worker_state`, accepting.
    63  
    64  The proof:
    65  
    66  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s `…_refines` lemmas walk the Rust runs
    67     into twin runs from the twin's own start state `AState.init EStore.empty`,
    68     related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/`AStateInv`: lockstep); `rust_stages`;
    69  2. **Theorem 1** — `Bridge/Stages.lean` takes the twin runs:
    70     `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` makes the check phase's accept con-leche's pure
    71     fold `checkDeclsPure` accepting the denoted stream at `streamEnv` of it;
    72  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a model,
    73     and `no_proof_of_False_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream.
    74  
    75  ## The named hypotheses
    76  
    77  The lemmas start from the binary's own start values (`startState` =
    78  `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`) and name the call the
    79  driver makes at each step.  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    80  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    81  they assume is exactly:
    82  
    83  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks: the driver
    84    parses with the verified reader loop `parse_source` over `FileChunks`, and
    85    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that `parse_chunks` over
    86    the chunks the reads hand out; the walk proves the reads are the file's bytes in
    87    the snapshot (`fileChunks_loop`);
    88  * on `--olean`, `hsnap : SnapshotOf finst fsv F` — the file instance answers as
    89    one snapshot `F`.
    90  
    91  `hpins` is the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list is what the verified
    92  decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems hold at every pin list);
    93  `model_exists_embedded` / `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded
    94  `PINS_TEXT`.
    95  -/

== crates/con-ron-core/src/driver/check_main.rs#L451-L525
   451  pub fn check_main<I: CheckerIo>(io: &mut I, a: &Args, file: &Vec<u32>) -> u8 {
   452      let verified = a.verified;
   453      let mode = if verified { CheckMode::Verified } else { CheckMode::Trusted };
   454      let mut st = AState::empty();
   455      let pers = PersTier::empty();
   456      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h1
   457      match pins::intern_reserved_pins(&pers, &mut st) {
   458          Err(e) => {
   459              io.note(&Note::ReservedPins(e, verified));
   460              return 3;
   461          }
   462          Ok(()) => (),
   463      }
   464      io.read_starts(&a.progress, file);
   465      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h2
   466      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(&pers, &mut st) {
   467          Err((e, line)) => {
   468              io.note(&Note::Prelude(e, line, verified));
   469              return 3;
   470          }
   471          Ok(p) => p,
   472      };
   473      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: hreads, h3
   474      let (read, err) = {
   475          let mut src = FileChunks { fs: &*io, path: file, off: 0, reads: 0, err: None };
   476          let read = export_c::parse_source(&pers, &mut st, &mut src);
   477          (read, src.err)
   478      };
   479      match err {
   480          Some(m) => {
   481              io.note(&Note::ReadFailed(str_copy(file), m));
   482              return 3;
   483          }
   484          None => (),
   485      }
   486      let parsed = match read {
   487          Err((e, line)) => {
   488              let c = exit_code(&e);
   489              io.note(&Note::Parse(e, line, str_copy(file), verified));
   490              return c;
   491          }
   492          Ok(p) => p,
   493      };
   494      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   495      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h4
   496      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(&pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls, &DeclUsedConsts) {
   497          Err(e) => {
   498              let c = exit_code(&e);
   499              io.note(&Note::Frontend(e, verified));
   500              return c;
   501          }
   502          Ok(p) => p,
   503      };
   504      if prepared.hoisted.len() > 0 {
   505          io.hoisted(&pers, &st.store, &prepared.hoisted);
   506      }
   507      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: hpins
   508      let pins: Vec<NatOpPinSet> = match embedded_pins(&*io) {
   509          None => return 3,
   510          Some(ps) => ps,
   511      };
   512      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h5
   513      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(&pers, &mut st, &pins, &a.max_nat_size) {
   514          Err(e) => {
   515              let c = exit_code(&e);
   516              io.note(&Note::Frontend(e, verified));
   517              return c;
   518          }
   519          Ok(p) => p,
   520      };
   521      let jobs: u64 = jobs_for_run(io, a);
   522      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h6, h7, h8
   523      let verdict = check_phase(io, &pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, None, &prepared.decls, jobs, file_records, prepared.synthesised);
   524      verdict_of(io, &pers, st, prepared.decls, verdict, file_records, verified)
   525  }

== crates/con-ron/src/std_io.rs#L1-L12
     1  //! `std_io` — the binary's instance of the core's `CheckerIo` (DESIGN.md §3.9,
     2  //! task #171): the file reads, the worker map, the escapes, and the rendering
     3  //! of every event the verified driver (`con_ron_core::driver`) hands it, in the
     4  //! binary's words.  All of it is outside the theorems, which are about the
     5  //! model instance (`proof/ConRon/MainTheorem/Model.lean`); what they assume of
     6  //! a run of this one is OVERVIEW §3.1: the file operations it performs answer
     7  //! as one snapshot (each path opened once, `olean_fs::RunFiles`), its maps' runs
     8  //! are an oracle's, its escapes write no file and do not end the process.
     9  //!
    10  //! The text of a usage error, of a help or a synopsis are the binary's
    11  //! (`bin/con-ron.rs`), handed in as `StdIoHooks`; the scheduler is
    12  //! `crate::modular::schedule`.

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L148-L185
   148  fn main() -> ! {
   149      let mut argv: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   150      for a in std::env::args_os().skip(1) {
   151          match a.into_string() {
   152              Ok(s) => argv.push(s),
   153              Err(_) => {
   154                  eprintln!("con-ron: an argument is not valid UTF-8");
   155                  exit_after_verdict(3)
   156              }
   157          }
   158      }
   159      let h = std::thread::Builder::new()
   160          .stack_size(driver::stack_bytes())
   161          .spawn(move || -> u8 {
   162              let cps: Vec<Vec<u32>> = argv.iter().map(|a| con_ron::render::cps(a)).collect();
   163              let mut io = con_ron::std_io::StdIo::new(con_ron::std_io::StdIoHooks {
   164                  help: print_help,
   165                  synopsis: print_synopsis,
   166                  usage: usage_error,
   167              });
   168              let code = con_ron_core::driver::cli::run_args(&mut io, &cps);
   169              // the instance (and what it kept) is never dropped: con-leche task #336
   170              exit_after_verdict(code)
   171          });
   172      match h {
   173          Err(e) => {
   174              eprintln!("con-ron: cannot spawn the checking thread: {}", e);
   175              exit_after_verdict(3)
   176          }
   177          Ok(h) => match h.join() {
   178              Ok(code) => exit_after_verdict(code),
   179              Err(_) => {
   180                  eprintln!("con-ron: the checking thread died");
   181                  exit_after_verdict(3)
   182              }
   183          },
   184      }
   185  }

== proof/ConRon/MainTheorem/Stages.lean#L196-L209
   196  structure SnapshotOf {Fs : Type} (inst : frontend.checker_io.CheckerFs Fs) (fsv : Fs)
   197      (F : ConLeche.FS) : Prop where
   198    path_exists : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.path_exists fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   199      b = (F.real q).isSome
   200    is_dir : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.is_dir fsv p = ok (.Ok b) → b = F.dir q
   201    real_path : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ r, inst.real_path fsv p = ok (.Ok r) →
   202      F.real q = some ⟨ConRon.Refine.absString r⟩ ∧ ConRon.Refine.StrWF r
   203    read_bin_file : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.read_bin_file fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   204      F.file q = some (absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b))
   205    read_range : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ off len b, inst.read_range fsv p off len = ok (.Ok b) →
   206      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b) =
   207        whole.extract off.val (min (off.val + len.val) whole.size)
   208    file_size : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ s, inst.file_size fsv p = ok (.Ok s) →
   209      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ s.val = whole.size

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Compare/Model.lean#L69-L76
    69  @[expose] def MixedStep (pinsP : List NatOpPinSet) (JS : Solution) (env : Env) (pd : Declaration)
    70      (env' : Env) : Prop :=
    71    (justifiable pd = none ∧
    72      ∃ F, ConLeche.checkDecl .verified (fueledOps .verified F) pinsP env pd = .ok env') ∨
    73    (∃ cv, justifiable pd = some cv ∧ env' = ⟨.axiomInfo cv :: env.consts, env.tables⟩ ∧
    74      justifyWhy JS (mkFEnv env) cv = none ∧ basisNamesOk pd = true ∧
    75      ∃ F, ConstantValRun F env cv cv.type)
    76

   299  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:256-298 CState
   300  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` — the checker
   301  /// state of (C): the arena, the per-call memo tables and — since task
   302  /// #97-P4c — the per-declaration caches (`whnfCore`, `whnf`, the two infer
   303  /// grades, `defeq`, the level verdicts, the instantiated constants).
   304  pub struct AState {
   305      pub store: EStore,
   306      pub memos: Memos,
   307      /// The per-DECLARATION caches (task #97-P4c, `arena::core_state`): the
   308      /// four entry-point memos (and `whnfCore`'s cheap mode's own), the
   309      /// `defeq` verdict table, the two level-verdict tables and the three lazy
   310      /// instantiated-constant tables.
   311      /// A record of its own beside `memos`, because the per-call clear and the
   312      /// per-declaration drop are different operations on different lifetimes.
   313      pub caches: Caches,
   314      /// The reserved-name pins (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the
   315      /// fifty-one constant names, the empty level list, the level `0` and
   316      /// `Sort 1`, interned ONCE into the persistent tier by the driver's
   317      /// `intern_all_pins` and read by handle ever after.  Empty until then,
   318      /// which is what makes a premature read a stop rather than a wrong
   319      /// answer (task #97c's hazard).
   320      pub pins: Pins,

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

  3613      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3614      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3615      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3616      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3617      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3618      ///
  3619      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3620      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3621      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3622      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3623      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3624      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3625      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3626      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3627      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3628      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3629      ///
  3630      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3631      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3632      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3633      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3634          match v {
  3635              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3636              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3637              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3638              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3639              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3640              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3641              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3642              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3643              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3644              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3645          }
  3646      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3897-L3944
  3897      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3898          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3899          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3900              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3901                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3902              } else {
  3903                  true
  3904              }
  3905          } else {
  3906              false
  3907          };
  3908          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3909              None
  3910          } else if pers.frozen {
  3911              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3912          } else {
  3913              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3914          };
  3915          match hit {
  3916              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3917              None => {
  3918                  if self.scratch_on {
  3919                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3920                      match at.1 {
  3921                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3922                          None => {
  3923                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3924                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3925                              } else {
  3926                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3927                                  let h: EIdx =
  3928                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3929                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3930                                  Ok(h)
  3931                              }
  3932                          }
  3933                      }
  3934                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3935                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3936                  } else {
  3937                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3938                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3939                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3940                      Ok(h)
  3941                  }
  3942              }
  3943          }
  3944      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L65-L88
    65  
    66  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
    67  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its worker reads the
    68  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Checker.lean`).
    69  /// **The persistent tier and the stream's index into a value**: the four
    70  /// persistent tables and the index move into one `PersTier` handed back
    71  /// `frozen`, for the workers to read (the index is the base `ifenv_find` reads
    72  /// below a job's own layer).  A pure MOVE: the store's scratch tiers and flags
    73  /// are untouched (a worker's store is its own, `worker_state`), and
    74  /// `thaw_tier` puts everything back where it was.  The driver's store is not
    75  /// read between the two.
    76  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore, ix: IStreamIndex) -> PersTier {
    77      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
    78      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
    79      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
    80      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
    81      PersTier {
    82          frozen: true,
    83          n,
    84          l,
    85          ls,
    86          e,
    87          env: ix,
    88      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1227-L1279
  1227  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:365-373 EStore
  1228  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1229  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1230  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1231  /// expressible.
  1232  ///
  1233  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1234  /// phase A's setup append to, and ONE flag, `scratch_on`.  **A store is in
  1235  /// one of two states, and "frozen" and "scratch on" are the same thing** (task
  1236  /// #98-FREEZE):
  1237  ///
  1238  /// * **owned, scratch off** (the parse, the setup, between phase A's
  1239  ///   declaration brackets): read through the EMPTY stand-in tier
  1240  ///   (`PersTier::empty`, `frozen` false), so every persistent read and every
  1241  ///   append goes to the owned field;
  1242  /// * **frozen, scratch on** (inside a declaration bracket, and a phase-B
  1243  ///   worker for its whole life): the owned field is empty — `freeze` moved it
  1244  ///   into a `PersTier` whose `frozen` bit is set — and the store is read
  1245  ///   through that tier, so every persistent read goes to it; every append is
  1246  ///   a SCRATCH append, so no append can reach a frozen persistent tier, by
  1247  ///   construction and not by a guard.
  1248  ///
  1249  /// Which tables a persistent read goes to is therefore the READER's to say
  1250  /// (`frozen`), not the store's: the choice is made by a value that is fixed
  1251  /// for the whole of a bracket or a worker, whatever runs inside it.  `freeze`
  1252  /// hands out a frozen tier and turns the scratch tier on; `thaw` takes it back
  1253  /// and turns it off; `empty_frozen` is a worker's store.  Promotion — the one
  1254  /// writer of the persistent tier inside a bracket — writes the frozen tier
  1255  /// itself, through `&mut PersTier` (`PersTier::intern_*`).
  1256  ///
  1257  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1258  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1259  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1260  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1261  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1262  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1263  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1264  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1265  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1266  pub struct PersTier {
  1267      /// This is a frozen store's tier: a store read through it reads its
  1268      /// persistent tables HERE.  `false` only for the empty stand-in an owned
  1269      /// store is handed (`PersTier::empty`), which is never read.
  1270      pub frozen: bool,
  1271      pub n: NTables,
  1272      pub l: LTables,
  1273      pub ls: LsTables,
  1274      pub e: ETables,
  1275      /// The stream's index, the frozen base of every job's environment
  1276      /// (`arena::env`'s `IFEnv` note): `checker::freeze_tier` moves it here, so
  1277      /// every worker reads one by reference.  Empty in every other tier.
  1278      pub env: IStreamIndex,
  1279  }

   749  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:189-218 FEnv
   750  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Env.lean:274-286 IFEnv` — the environment
   751  /// with its `O(1)` index (DESIGN.md §8.3 lesson 13), over the frozen base of a
   752  /// stream's index, and the two literal flags of its lookups.  con-leche's `ovl`
   753  /// field is not ported (see `ifenv_find`).
   754  ///
   755  /// **The environment has two tiers, like the store.**  An `IFEnv` is one LAYER:
   756  /// a job's own, empty until its record pushes.  The BASE is the stream's index
   757  /// (`arena::stream_index::IStreamIndex`), built once before any check and
   758  /// frozen into the `PersTier` (`checker::freeze_tier`), where every worker reads
   759  /// it by reference.  The layer's own entries are all visible (con-leche's local
   760  /// index has no counter); the base is read below the layer's two bounds,
   761  /// con-leche's `FBase.below` and `FBase.belowRec`, which live here because the
   762  /// base itself is shared.
   763  ///
   764  /// **The index row is a SLOT and not an `IConstantInfo`** (task #97-P6-5,
   765  /// lever 1): the twin's row carries the constant itself, a shared value in Lean
   766  /// and a second deep copy in Rust.  Every writer keeps `idx` and `env.consts`
   767  /// in step (`ifenv_push`, `ifenv_push_temp`, `ifenv_pop_temp`) and
   768  /// `ifenv_find` reads `env.consts[s]`.  The table map `tbls` is built the same
   769  /// way: its row is the table's slot in `env.tables`.
   770  pub struct IFEnv {
   771      pub env: IEnv,
   772      pub idx: HashMap<NIdx, u64>,
   773      pub tbls: HashMap<NIdx, u64>,
   774      /// The base's constants are visible below this counter (`FBase.below`).
   775      pub base_below: u64,
   776      /// The base's tables are visible below this record position
   777      /// (`FBase.belowRec`).
   778      pub base_below_rec: u64,

   780      /// reads it at every literal it meets, so it is set where the layer is made
   781      /// and kept by every push.
   782      pub nat_lit: bool,
   783      /// **Are string literals expandable** here (`str_lit_stored_by`), as
   784      /// `nat_lit`.
   785      pub str_lit: bool,
   786  }

   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/ExprOpsC.lean:2409-2413 allLevelParamsDefinedC
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:666-668 constsResolveFC
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron-core/src/driver/check_main.rs#L451-L525
   451  pub fn check_main<I: CheckerIo>(io: &mut I, a: &Args, file: &Vec<u32>) -> u8 {
   452      let verified = a.verified;
   453      let mode = if verified { CheckMode::Verified } else { CheckMode::Trusted };
   454      let mut st = AState::empty();
   455      let pers = PersTier::empty();
   456      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h1
   457      match pins::intern_reserved_pins(&pers, &mut st) {
   458          Err(e) => {
   459              io.note(&Note::ReservedPins(e, verified));
   460              return 3;
   461          }
   462          Ok(()) => (),
   463      }
   464      io.read_starts(&a.progress, file);
   465      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h2
   466      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(&pers, &mut st) {
   467          Err((e, line)) => {
   468              io.note(&Note::Prelude(e, line, verified));
   469              return 3;
   470          }
   471          Ok(p) => p,
   472      };
   473      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: hreads, h3
   474      let (read, err) = {
   475          let mut src = FileChunks { fs: &*io, path: file, off: 0, reads: 0, err: None };
   476          let read = export_c::parse_source(&pers, &mut st, &mut src);
   477          (read, src.err)
   478      };
   479      match err {
   480          Some(m) => {
   481              io.note(&Note::ReadFailed(str_copy(file), m));
   482              return 3;
   483          }
   484          None => (),
   485      }
   486      let parsed = match read {
   487          Err((e, line)) => {
   488              let c = exit_code(&e);
   489              io.note(&Note::Parse(e, line, str_copy(file), verified));
   490              return c;
   491          }
   492          Ok(p) => p,
   493      };
   494      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   495      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h4
   496      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(&pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls, &DeclUsedConsts) {
   497          Err(e) => {
   498              let c = exit_code(&e);
   499              io.note(&Note::Frontend(e, verified));
   500              return c;
   501          }
   502          Ok(p) => p,
   503      };
   504      if prepared.hoisted.len() > 0 {
   505          io.hoisted(&pers, &st.store, &prepared.hoisted);
   506      }
   507      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: hpins
   508      let pins: Vec<NatOpPinSet> = match embedded_pins(&*io) {
   509          None => return 3,
   510          Some(ps) => ps,
   511      };
   512      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h5
   513      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(&pers, &mut st, &pins, &a.max_nat_size) {
   514          Err(e) => {
   515              let c = exit_code(&e);
   516              io.note(&Note::Frontend(e, verified));
   517              return c;
   518          }
   519          Ok(p) => p,
   520      };
   521      let jobs: u64 = jobs_for_run(io, a);
   522      // ConRon.MainTheorem.Stages: h6, h7, h8
   523      let verdict = check_phase(io, &pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, None, &prepared.decls, jobs, file_records, prepared.synthesised);
   524      verdict_of(io, &pers, st, prepared.decls, verdict, file_records, verified)
   525  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the
    22  //! pin list (the embedded one, decoded) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-two names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

   186  pub fn intern_all_pins(

   189      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,

   191  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {

   198                  Err(e) => Err(e),
   199                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   200              },
   201          },

   286  pub struct FileChunks<'a, F: CheckerFs> {
   287      /// the file operations
   288      pub fs: &'a F,
   289      /// the file
   290      pub path: &'a Vec<u32>,
   291      /// where the next read starts: the bytes handed out so far
   292      pub off: u64,
   293      /// the reads that answered so far: a `usize`, so that the chunks they
   294      /// handed out are a list a `usize` indexes (`Vec<Vec<u8>>`, the form the
   295      /// staged lemmas' `parse_chunks` is stated over) on every platform
   296      pub reads: usize,
   297      /// the first read failure, if any
   298      pub err: Option<Vec<u32>>,
   299  }
   300  
   301  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:210-218 foldChunks
   302  impl<'a, F: CheckerFs> ChunkSource for FileChunks<'a, F> {
   303      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:210-218 foldChunks
   304      /// One read of up to `CHUNK_SIZE` bytes at the offset; empty at the end or
   305      /// on a failure, and empty for good after a failure.
   306      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   307          match &self.err {
   308              Some(_) => return Vec::new(),
   309              None => (),
   310          }
   311          match self.fs.read_range(self.path, self.off, CHUNK_SIZE as u64) {
   312              Ok(b) => {
   313                  self.off = self.off + (b.len() as u64);
   314                  self.reads = self.reads + 1;
   315                  b
   316              }
   317              Err(e) => {
   318                  self.err = Some(e);
   319                  Vec::new()
   320              }
   321          }
   322      }
   323  }

   178  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StreamIndex.lean:64-66 buildIndex
   179  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:57-75 Jobs.build
   180  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/StreamIndex.lean:102-105 buildIndex` — **the frozen
   181  /// index of a stream**, the records folded in order from `i` on and the index
   182  /// frozen past the last (`stream_index_freeze`, con-leche's `Jobs.build`).  An
   183  /// `Err` is the store's own failure (a term the install builds could not be
   184  /// interned) or an unfilled pin table, never a verdict about the stream; it
   185  /// carries the position of the record whose reading failed (past the last for
   186  /// the freeze), for the error line.  A solution's index (con-leche's `Jobs.side`) is the same build over the solution's records (`justify::solution_of`).
   187  ///
   188  /// **A loop**, one iteration per record: the cited `foldlM` is a loop in Lean,
   189  /// and Rust does not promise to eliminate the tail call (a solution of 1.47 M
   190  /// records overflowed a 1 GiB stack, task #167).  Every exit is a `return`, so
   191  /// the extracted `build_index_loop` is the recursion one for one.
   192  pub fn build_index(
   193      pers: &PersTier,
   194      st: &mut AState,
   195      ix: IStreamIndex,
   196      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   197      i: usize,
   198  ) -> Result<IStreamIndex, (CheckError, u64)> {
   199      let mut ix: IStreamIndex = ix;
   200      let mut i: usize = i;
   201      loop {
   202          if i >= ds.len() {
   203              return match stream_index_freeze(st, ix) {
   204                  Err(e) => Err((e, i as u64)),
   205                  Ok(fx) => Ok(fx),
   206              };
   207          }
   208          match stream_index_add(pers, st, ix, &ds[i]) {
   209              Err(e) => return Err((e, i as u64)),
   210              Ok(ix2) => {
   211                  ix = ix2;
   212                  i = i + 1;
   213              }
   214          }
   215      }
   216  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/driver/check_main.rs#L177-L222
   177  pub fn olean_job<F: CheckerFs>(
   178      fs: &F,
   179      tier: &PersTier,
   180      w: &mut AState,
   181      cache: &mut ValueCache,
   182      mode: &CheckMode,
   183      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   184      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   185      pk: &OleanPins,
   186      values: &Vec<ModRef>,
   187      sp: &Roots,
   188      sol: Option<&Solution>,
   189      k: usize,
   190  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> {
   191      let ku = k as u64;
   192      if k >= ds.len() {
   193          return checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, sol, ds, ku);
   194      }
   195      match &ds[k] {
   196          IDeclaration::ThmDecl(cv, v) => {
   197              // a theorem's value is a reference only if its handle is a `bvar`: the
   198              // store's projection reads the bvar table at the handle's slot whatever
   199              // its tag
   200              let code: Option<u64> = if v.tag() == ETAG_BVAR { w.store.view_bvar(tier, v) } else { None };
   201              match code {
   202                  None => checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, sol, ds, ku),
   203                  Some(code) => {
   204                      enter_record(w);
   205                      let r = match records::read_value(fs, pk, tier, &mut w.store, sp, values, cache, code) {
   206                          Err(e) => Err((e, ku)),
   207                          Ok(v) => {
   208                              let pd = IDeclaration::ThmDecl(env::i_constant_val_dup(cv), v);
   209                              match stream_index::record_check(tier, w, mode, pins, sol, ku, &pd) {
   210                                  Err(e) => Err((e, ku)),
   211                                  Ok(()) => Ok(()),
   212                              }
   213                          }
   214                      };
   215                      leave_record(w);
   216                      r
   217                  }
   218              }
   219          }
   220          _ => checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, sol, ds, ku),
   221      }
   222  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/driver/check_main.rs#L308-L345
   308  pub fn check_phase<I: CheckerIo>(
   309      io: &mut I,
   310      pers: &PersTier,
   311      st: &mut AState,
   312      mode: &CheckMode,
   313      ipins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   314      sol: Option<&Solution>,
   315      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   316      jobs: u64,
   317      file_records: usize,
   318      synthesised: u64,
   319  ) -> Result<IStreamIndex, (CheckError, u64)> {
   320      io.index_starts();
   321      let ix = match stream_index::build_index(pers, st, stream_index::stream_index_empty(), ds, 0) {
   322          Err(e) => return Err(e),
   323          Ok(ix) => ix,
   324      };
   325      io.parse_done(pers, &st.store, ds.len(), file_records, synthesised);
   326      let n = ds.len();
   327      let workers = workers_for(jobs, n);
   328      io.check_starts(n, workers);
   329      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, ix);
   330      let r = {
   331          let step = JobStep { tier: &tier, mode, pins: ipins, apins: &st.pins, sol, ds };
   332          io.par_map_workers(&step, n, workers)
   333      };
   334      let ix: IStreamIndex = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   335      match r {
   336          Ok(()) => {
   337              io.check_done(n, &None);
   338              Ok(ix)
   339          }
   340          Err((e, pos)) => {
   341              io.check_done(n, &Some(pos));
   342              Err((e, pos))
   343          }
   344      }
   345  }

    35  //!
    36  //! ## What a worker is, in the check phase
    37  //!
    38  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what the check phase is: "the persistent tier is
    39  //! immutable, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**"
    40  //! (`record_job` is the bracket; nothing writes the persistent tier after the
    41  //! index is built and frozen, and a worker never holds it `&mut`).  So the
    42  //! driver's `init`
    43  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    44  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    45  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    46  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier`, which
    47  //! holds the stream's index.  A job reads it through an empty layer of its own
    48  //! at its record's view and pushes into that layer.  So a worker costs no

   123  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:65-73 AState.worker` — the twin's
   124  /// worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   125  /// **A worker's start state** (the cited `init`): the empty store, FROZEN
   126  /// (`EStore::empty_frozen`, task #98-FREEZE), so that every persistent read goes
   127  /// to the `PersTier` the boundary froze and every append is a scratch append;
   128  /// fresh memos and caches; and a copy of the pins, the run's maximum `Nat` size
   129  /// among them (con-leche's `checkPool mode maxNatSize`, which hands it to every
   130  /// job's fresh state through `runAt` and `recordJob`).  The store stays frozen for
   131  /// the worker's life: `record_job` only empties its scratch tier.  A run with a solution builds the same state: the solution is handed to every
   132  /// job (`run_job`), not kept in the worker.

   135      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L233-L294
   233  }
   234  
   235  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:486-512 parMapWorkersIO
   236  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:211-239 checkPool
   237  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   238  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   239  ///
   240  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker,
   241  /// > each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step` over its
   242  /// > claimed indices in claim order, which is increasing, and every step
   243  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   244  ///
   245  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   246  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   247  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   248  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   249  ///
   250  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `stack_bytes()` of stack each.
   251  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   252  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   253  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   254  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   255  /// not depend on it.
   256  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   257      n: usize,
   258      workers: usize,
   259      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   260      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   261      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   262  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {
   263      let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
   264      let limit = AtomicUsize::new(n);
   265      let run = || worker(n, &next, &limit, &init, &step, &after);
   266      let mut results: Vec<Vec<(usize, Result<(), E>)>> = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   267      let mut panicked = false;
   268      std::thread::scope(|scope| {
   269          let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   270          for w in 0..workers {
   271              let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
   272                  .stack_size(stack_bytes())
   273                  .name(format!("check-{}", w))
   274                  .spawn_scoped(scope, &run);
   275              match spawned {
   276                  Ok(h) => handles.push(h),
   277                  // Out of threads, or out of address space for another stack:
   278                  // run on the workers already spawned (the module note).
   279                  Err(_) => break,
   280              }
   281          }
   282          if handles.is_empty() {
   283              results.push(run());
   284          }
   285          for h in handles {
   286              match h.join() {
   287                  Ok(rs) => results.push(rs),
   288                  Err(_) => panicked = true,
   289              }
   290          }
   291      });
   292      if panicked {
   293          return Err(ParallelError::Panicked);
   294      }

   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:376-504 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204

   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/
    73  @[expose] def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Rel.lean#L61-L78
    61  /-! ## The core grade -/
    62  
    63  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    64  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    65  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    66  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    67  theorem PStep.toCore {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    68      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK false env fe s) : CoreStep env fe s s' :=
    69    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩
    70  
    71  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/Cached/SimC.lean:366 SimC — **the CORE grade's
    72  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    73  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    74  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/
    75  @[expose] def CSpec (env : Env) (fe : IFEnv) {α : Type}
    76      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=
    77    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), CheckOK false env fe s₀ → P s₀.store →
    78      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L128-L174
   128  /-! ## The spines -/
   129  
   130  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   131  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   132  
   133  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   134  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   135  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   136  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   137  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   138      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   139      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   140        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   141    intro n
   142    induction n with
   143    | zero =>
   144      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   145      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   146      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   147      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   148    | succ n ih =>
   149      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   150      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   151      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   152      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   153      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   154      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   155      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   156      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   157      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   158          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   159            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   160        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   161        congr 1
   162        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   163        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   164        congr 1
   165        omega
   166      rw [hkey]
   167      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   168  
   169  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   170      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   171    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   172    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   173    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   174    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

    68      ∀ f {eager : Bool}, KnotSpec eager env fe f
